In [[mathematics]], the '''Hadamard gap theorem''' is a result about the [[analytic continuation]] of [[Lacunary function|lacunary]] [[power series]]. Such a power series is "badly behaved" in the sense that it cannot be extended to be an [[analytic function]] anywhere on the [[Boundary (topology)|boundary]] of its [[Radius of convergence|disk of convergence]]. The result was proved by [[Jacques Hadamard]] in his influencial 1892 [[thesis]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hadamard |first=J. |date=1892 |title=Essai sur l'étude des fonctions données par leur développement de Taylor |url=https://www.numdam.org/item/?id=JMPA_1892_4_8__101_0 |journal=Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées |language=fr |volume=8 |pages=101–186 |issn=1776-3371}}</ref>

==Statement of the theorem==

Let  <math>0<n_0<n_1<\dots</math> be a [[sequence]] of [[Integer|integers]] such that the <math>n_{k+1}/n_k \ge \lambda > 1</math> for <math>k \ge 0</math>, or equivalently<math display="block">\liminf_{k\to\infty} \frac{n_{k+1}}{n_k} > 1.</math>Let <math>(a_k)_{k\ge0}</math> be a sequence of complex numbers such that the power series

: <math>f(z) = \sum_{k=0}^\infty a_k z^{n_k}</math>

has [[radius of convergence]] <math>1</math>. Then the unit circle is a [[natural boundary]] for the series ''<math>f</math>''.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Titchmarsh |first=E. C. |title=The Theory of Functions |date=1939 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=|pages=223}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Dienes |first=Paul |title=The Taylor Series: An Introduction to the Theory of Functions of a Complex Variable |publisher=Dover Publications |year=1957 |pages=231}}</ref>

This theorem is a special case of both the [[Fabry gap theorem]] and [[Ostrowski's overconvergence theorem]].
